title: coding languages
text:
HTML - Content & Layout
HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) is used to create the ‘bones’ of a website. It provides structure to a web page using text and visual formatting. When written properly, it should also be able to define the meaning of the content within the web page in a machine-readable way, which is vital for accessibility and search engine optimization.

title: coding languages
text:
CSS - Aesthetics
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is used to define the style of a web page. Think of any website’s design, layout, or how it varies between devices. I like to think of CSS as the clothing of the web page’s proverbial body. If a website looks the same on every device we will quickly run into scaling problems when using a smaller device, such as a phone. I’ve run into an issue where a web page that works completely fine on computer, but barely functions on mobile because of improper formatting, and when this page does function it is because I am zooming in and scrolling endlessly from side to side. CSS prevents these problems if the programmer remembers to make a separate layout for mobile devices.

title: coding languages
text:
JavaScript - Interactive Elements
JavaScript is a programming language used to create dynamic content for websites. It achieves this by adding new HTML elements while modifying existing ones. Any time a web page has a drop down menu or a bar that pops out from the side that is an example of JavaScript. Anything clickable is also JavaScript.

title: coding languages
text:
PHP
PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is an open-source, server-side programming language that is cross-platform and fairly easy to learn. PHP can be used to create websites, applications, customer relationship management systems and more. It is a widely-used general-purpose language that can be embedded into HTML.

title: interactive mockup software
section: What Is An Interactive Mockup Software
text:
What Is An Interactive Mockup Software
Interactive Mockup software is utilized to create digital prototypes that allow the users to see how their website, product, or app will function or appear. Users of these interactive mockups can click buttons, scroll through pages, and navigate through different screens to see how an idea or design would behave in real life. Users can also test their designs and check for potential issues and can make adjustments before development starts. Some good interactive mockup softwares to look into are figma, Adobe XD, Penpot, and Framer.

Figma
Figma, a cloud based tool that allows users to create wireframes, Uis, and prototypes, has collaboration features and can be used to hand off designs to developers once designing is complete. Figma’s primary strength is its ability to create interactive prototypes that designers can link different screens, set triggers to do actions like clicks or hovers, and add transitions between states that simulate user navigation. Figma also allows designers to work on the same design at the same time, making collaboration easy with real time feedback. Users of figma can create high-fidelity mockups with detailed visuals to closely resemble a product.


Adobe XD
Adobe XD is also very useful when creating Mockups as it is a vector based tool that allows users to create prototypes of web applications. Adobe XD’s main focus is to create interactive prototypes where users can click through different screens to see how a design would actually work. Users can connect screens to create navigation flows within a prototype. Once these prototypes are created, they can be easily shared with clients and stakeholders for feedback and approval.


Penpot
Another good software to look into is Penpot, which allows its users to create interactive mockups and prototypes as well. Penpot works as an open source which means the software is freely accessible and customizable by the community. It has a collaborative design which allows for multiple users to work on a design simultaneously, making it an ideal choice for team projects. Penpot generates code snippets directly from the design which reduces the need for manual translation. It also allows for creation and management of design systems with reusable components.


Framer
Framer is also a good option as it allows designers to create high-fidelity, clickable prototypes of websites and applications without needing a code. With no code prototyping, users can design and build interactive prototypes with visual interference, without complex coding. Its advanced interactions make it easy to add animations, transitions, and complex user interactions to your prototypes. Framer offers a canvas similar to other designs like figma, allowing you to import assets and create layers with ease, It also offers collaboration features to allows for designers and stakeholders to collaborate in real time.

text:
Features
There are many features to this tool but the most common ones include debugging web pages, learning and experimentation, and web design inspiration.
During the debugging process you can identify issues which allows developers to quickly find and fix issues without layout, styles, or scripts by inspecting elements and viewing any related CSS and JavaScript. You can also located console errors which can display JavaScript errors and warnings, helping developers troubleshoot issues.
With learning and experimentations a user can do two types: CSS experimentation and HTML structure. CSS experimentation, users can modify CSS properties live to see how changes affect the design without permanently altering the code. With HTML structure it allows learners to understand the structure of a webpage, including how elements are nested and styled.
Using this tool with web design inspiration you can access copying styles and color and font identification. Users can inspect a website to see how specific styles are applied, which can inspire their own designs or help replicate certain effects while searching for copying styles. Color and font indentification can easily identify colors, fonts, and sizes used on a webpage, which is useful for design projects.

title: inspect element
text:
How to Access
There are many different ways to access “Inspect Element”, some more difficult then others but they all lead to the same place.
It also depends on what device you are using to access this tool. Some systems may not have the same features as others do. The most common electronics used to access the “Inspect Element” tool are a Windows/Linux or a Mac.
Accessing the “Inspect Element” may also be different depending in what webpage you are using. Whether it is Chrome, Firefox, or Safari, you will be able to find a way to access this tool.

Access on Chrome

Method 1:
Right-click anywhere on the webpage, and at the very bottom of the menu that pops up, click Inspect.


Method 2:
Click the hamburger menu (the icon with three stacked dots) on the far-right of your Google Chrome toolbar, click More Tools, then select Developer Tools.


Method 3:
Press command + option + I on a Mac, or Ctrl + Shift on a PC to open “Inspect Element” without clicking anything



Access on Firefox

Method 1:
Right-click anywhere on the page and click Inspect at the bottom of the menu.


Method 2:
Click the hamburger menu (three horizontal lines at the top-right corner of the window), select More Tools, then click Web Developer Tools


Method 3:
The keyboard shortcut on Firefox is command + option + I for Macs and Control + Shift + C for PCs.



Access on Safari

Click the Safari dropdown in the top navigation bar above the Safari window, and then click Preferences.
Navigate to Advanced, and check the box at the bottom of the window by Show Develop menu in the menu bar. Close the window.
Now, you should be able to right-click anywhere on the page and click Inspect Element to open the Elements pane.
The pane should appear along the bottom of your window. To move it to a side alignment and give yourself a little more space to look at the code, click the Dock to right of window (or left of window) option on the top-left of the pane, next to the “X”

How do VPNs benefit people?
VPNS encrypting their internet traffic and masking their IP address, effectively hiding their online activity and location, providing increased privacy and security when browsing the web, especially on public Wi-Fi networks; it allows users to access geo-restricted conten and potentially avoid online surveillantce or tracking by third parties.


Do VPNS fully protect my information?
A VPN may boast strong protocols and military-grade encryption, but that doesn’t mean it’s infallible. It can’t prevent cookie tracking, viruses, or malware, and it can’t protect against phishing scams. Data leaks could occur. But most pivotally, a VPN is only as secure as the company that runs it. A VPN provider that uses out-of-date protocols, leaks IPs, and logs your data isn’t one you can trust. No VPN can guarantee absolute security, though choosing a reliable one will make a whole lot of difference with web surfing.

title: No-Code Site Builders
section: What is no code site builder
text:
What is no code site builder
No-code site builders are tools that allow users to create websites without needing to write any code. These platforms use visual interfaces with drag-and-drop features, making it easy for anyone, regardless of their technical skill level, to design and launch a website. Users can choose from pre-built templates, customize layouts and integrate various functionalities such as forms, e-commerce options, and social media links, all without having to learn programming languages like HTML, CSS, or javaScript. No-code site builders empower individuals and businesses to create professional websites quickly and efficiently.

title: No-Code Site Builders
text:
No-Code for Google sites
Google Sites is a user friendly platform designed to help individuals and businesses create websites without the need for coding knowledge. It caters to users who want to build websites quickly and efficiently, offering a straightforward drag-and-drop interface. With Google sites, users can choose from various templates to jumpstart their projects, whether it’s a simple portfolio, a personal blog, or a team collaboration site. This makes it an excellent tool for beginners or those looking to create a web presence without hiring a developer.
The beauty of Google Sites lies in its simplicity and integration with other Google services. Since it connects seamlessly with Google Drive, users can easily embed content like documents, slides, and spreadsheets directly into their website. This is particularly useful for businesses or educational purposes where collaboration and easy access to shared resources are important. Additionally, the platform automatically adjusts for mobile responsiveness, ensuring that websites look good on any device without extra effort from the user.
Although Google Sites is a powerful no-code tool, it does have limitations when it comes to customization. Users are restricted to the built-in templates and design options, meaning those looking for more complex or visually unique websites might find it less flexible compared to other platforms like WordPress or Wix. Still, its ease of use and streamlined functionality make it ideal for people who prioritize simplicity over highly custom designs or advanced features.

title: No-Code Site Builders
text:
No-Code for Wix
Wix is one of the most popular no-code website builders on the market, known for its user-friendly interface and vast array of design options, It allows users to create professional websites without needing any coding knowledge. With its drag-and-drop functionality, Wix provides an intuitive platform that can be easily navigated by beginners, yet it also offers advanced features for more experienced users. Whether you want to build a personal blog, an online store, or a business website, Wix offers the flexibility to bring your vision to life.
One of Wix’s standout features is its large section of pre-designed templates. These templates cater to a wide range of industries, including e-commerce, photography, hospitality, and more. Users can select a template that fits their needs and then customize it by changing fonts, colors, and layouts.The drag-and-drop editor allows for quick adjustments, making the process of building a site fast and simple. Additionally, Wix’s templates are responsive, meaning they automatically adjust to look good on any device, from desktops to smartphones.
Wix also integrates a wide variety of apps and third-party tools that extend the platform’s functionality. These apps cover everything from social media integration to advanced SEO tools, booking systems, and payment getaways. For users who want to expand their site’s capabilities, the Wix App Market offers a way to integrate these features without having to write any code. These app marketplace continually evolves, ensuring that users can access the latest tools to enhance their websites.
Furthermore, Wix has solid customer support options, including live chat, phone support, and an extensive knowledge base. The platform’s comprehensive help center offers step-by-step guides and video tutorials to help users solve any issues they might encounter. Wix also provides a free plan for users to explore the platform and start building their websites without any entail investment. For those looking for more advanced features, Wix offers premium plans with additional storages, professional domains, and e-commerce capabilities, making it a flexible solution for all types of users.

title: No-Code Site Builders
text:
No-Code for Webflow
Webflow is a powerful no-code website builder designed for both beginners and advanced users. While it’s known for its visual web design capabilities, Webflow provides a level of customization that typically requires coding, all within a no-code environment. This makes it a popular choice for designers who want more control over their websites without writing any code. Webflow’s interface allows users to design responsive websites by dragging and stopping elements, with precise control over layouts, typography, animations, and interactions. It combines the ease of no-code tools with the flexibility typically found in more technical web design platforms.
One of Webflow’s key strengths is its robust design and customization options. The platform allows for pixel-perfect design, making it possible to create highly unique and visually stunning websites. With its CS grid and flexbox support, users can create complex responsive layouts that adapt to any screen size without the need for custom code. Additionally, Webflow’s interactions and animations tools enable users to create dynamic effects, such as scroll-based animations and hover interactions, without touching any code. These features make it an attractive option for designers looking to bring their creative ideas to life in a no-code environment.
Webflow also stands out with its intergrade CMS( Content Management System), which allows users to build dynamic, content-rich websites. The CMS enables users to create custom collections (like blogs, portfolios, or product catalogs) and easily manage content across options for businesses, agencies, and content creators who want to scale their sites while maintaining flexibility. The platform also supports e-commerce, making it easy to launch an online store with custom product pages, shopping carts, and checkout processes. Webflow’s ecommerce capabilities are customizable, allowing users to build fully tailored shopping experiences without needing any coding skills.
Additionally, Webflow offers excellent hosting and SEO features, which are essential for any websites looking to perform well in search engines. Webflow’s hosting in fast, secure, and reliable, with built-in features like SSL certificates, site backups, and global CDN (Content Delivery Network) support. Its SEO tools allow users to optimize their site’s metadata, URLs, and alt tags directly with the platform, making it easier to rank on search engines. Webflow also provides detailed analytics and the option to export clean, exportable code for developers who may want to make further customizations down the line. With these powerful features, Webflow has positioned itself as a top choice for those seeking a flexible, no-code platform that can grow with their needs.

title: bandwidth
text:
How does bandwidth work?
Network bandwidth works by determining how much data can be transmitted over a connection at any given time. Think of it like a highway—just as more lanes allow more cars to pass through at once, higher bandwidth allows more data to flow simultaneously. When you send or receive data (like streaming a video or downloading a file), your device breaks the data into packets, which travel across the network to their destination. The speed at which these packets move depends on bandwidth availability. If the network is congested or your connection has limited bandwidth, data packets take longer to arrive, causing buffering or lag. Bandwidth is shared among all devices on a network, so the more devices using it at once, the slower each connection may be.

title: internet
text:
Basic Structure of The Internet
The internet is essentially a network of networks. It’s made up of countless devices (computers, smartphones, servers, etc.) all connected through wired (fiber-optic, copper cables) and wireless (Wi-Fi, satellites) technologies. At its core, the internet relies on a series of backbones — these are high-speed, long-distance data routes, usually run by large telecom companies or governments, that connect smaller local networks. When you access the internet from home, your device is communicating with these backbone networks through your Internet Service Provider (ISP), which might be companies like Comcast, AT&T, or Verizon to name a few.

title: internet
text:
Protocols of the Internet
The internet’s servers allow devices to communicate and share information. It relies on a system of protocols like IP (Internet Protocol) for addressing devices, TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) for breaking down and reassembling data, and HTTP/HTTPS for transferring web content. Every device has a unique IP address, and the Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable web addresses (like “www.google.com”) into these numerical addresses.

title: internet
section: How Data is Transmitted and Websites Work
text:
How Data is Transmitted and Websites Work
Data is transmitted through a complex path, where packets travel across routers and servers until they reach their destination. Websites and online services are hosted on web servers, which store and manage the content that you access. Browsers like Chrome or Safari interpret the data sent from these servers, displaying it as websites using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

title: internet
text:
The Infrastructure Behind the Internet
The infrastructure behind the internet includes both physical elements, like fiber-optic cables and wireless technologies (Wi-Fi, cellular), and a variety of organizations that manage how data flows. Entities like ICANN oversee domain names, while Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) ensure fast data delivery by distributing website content to servers around the world. Cloud services also play a huge role in storing and processing data remotely, making it accessible from any device.

title: internet
section: The Internet’s Evolution and Security Concern
text:
The Internet’s Evolution and Security Concern
As the internet has evolved, it’s become central to nearly every aspect of modern life, powering everything from social media to e-commerce, online learning, and entertainment. While the internet offers tremendous benefits, it also brings security and privacy risks, with concerns about hacking, data breaches, and surveillance. Encryption and secure browsing protocols (like HTTPS) help mitigate some of these risks, but staying vigilant online remains important.

title: Internet Privacy
text:
Intro
The standard definition of privacy incorporates two important elements: the state of being alone and not being watched or interrupted by other people. When you’re scrolling on social media, you may be physically alone, but you’re being watched through the internet. This can be very scary to many. This illusion of privacy is just that, an illusion. Today, let’s talk about the importance of online privacy, and how to protect yourself from online dangers.

title: Internet Privacy
text:
Importance
You probably don’t want thieves to know where you live, or the exact time you’re not home. You don’t want to give scammers a chance to use your date, place of birth, and other personal data to take out loans in your name. These cyber-criminals can access your most personal information and use it against you, and most of the time, there’s nothing you can do about it. Every time you sign up for a new app or make a purchase online, you are agreeing with a set of terms and conditions. Your agreement means organizations can legally collect information about you. Although this collection of personal information is legal, it doesn’t mean you can’t take steps to limit this invasion of privacy.

title: Internet Privacy
section: How You’re Allowing People to Scam You
text:
How You’re Allowing People to Scam You
You’re probably allowing scammers to access your data everyday, and here’s how: reusing weak passwords is one of the leading causes for the massive data breaches you see in the news. Weak passwords allow cyber criminals to break into multiple accounts at once and engage in identity theft or financial fraud. Oversharing provides information to malicious onlookers. Posting videos of your home can give a map of your belongings and how to access them. Taking pictures of your boarding passes can reveal how long you’ll be away and where you’ll be traveling. Every post could create a clear picture of your life, habits, relationships, and possessions. Cyber-criminals can steal information from you through malicious extensions, infected ads, scam links that lead to scam websites, and much more. They could bait you into opening deceiving emails, taping links in misleading messages, or even get personal data in fake phone calls. They can collect your usernames and passwords, which would allow them to steal your money, access confidential information, or turn your life into a living nightmare.

title: Internet Privacy
section: How to Protect Your Internet Privacy
text:
How to Protect Your Internet Privacy
Good thing there are ways to avoid such invasions. You could set up an early-warning system that patrols the internet for you. These services monitor your digital footprint, starting with your email address and phone number. They will alert you if your personal data is leaked in new breaches through privacy threats. Try to provide as little information about yourself as possible, every time you’re asked to provide information, consider the risks and benefits. Get educated about laws and regulations or other measures that impact your online privacy, and advocate for the ones you support. Change your passwords frequently, and make them hard to guess. Try to avoid adding personal information in your password, such as specific dates, as they’re easy to guess. Consider using a phrase that you will remember easily, something that only you would know. Use different passwords for different sites, so that if one is breached, the others will not be affected. Try not to get caught in the phishing net. If you don’t recognize a number or the sender of an email, don’t fall for it. Get rid of apps and browsers that you don’t use, because many apps make money from collecting your personal user data, keep that in mind when you download them. Use a secure VPN(Virtual Private Network) while you’re browsing online. This essentially encodes your information, and makes it unreadable to hackers. I’m sure you’ve opened a website and have clicked “accept cookies” without even knowing what cookies are. They’re small text files that store information about you and be used to track your movements across multiple sites. You should disable third-party cookies, delete cookies when you quit a browser, and make exceptions for individual sites. Those are just a few ways you can protect your personal data.

title: intro
text:
Networks
A Network refers to an interconnected computing device. These networks can share resources and data. A networked device can use a system of rules, these rules are called communication protocols and transmit information over physical or wireless technologies. A network can work through nodes and links, these are the basic building blocks in computer networking. A network node may be data communication equipment, also known as DCE, examples of this would be a modem, hub, or switch. A node could also be a data terminal equipment (DTE), this would consist of two or more computers/ printers. A link refers to the transmission media that connects two nodes. Links could be something physical such as a wire or optical fiber, or they may be free space used by wireless networks.

title: intro
text:
Transmission Control Protocol
Transmission Control Protocol, or TCP, is used to organize data; it does this by ensuring secure transmission between the server and the client. TCP, regardless of the amount of data, guarantees integrity when it’s sent over the network. Because of this, it is used to transmit data from higher-level protocols that require all transmitted data to arrive. The underlying protocol behind many applications is TCP, this includes file and data transfers, email, and peer-to-peer sharing. TCP is connection-oriented, meaning that a connection is established and is maintained until all applications have finished exchanging messages.

title: intro
text:
HTTP
The Hypertext Protocol, better known as HTTP, is the foundation of the World Wide Web, it’s made to load web pages through hypertext links. HTTP is an application layer protocol that can transfer information between networked devices, and run on top of other layers of the network protocol stack. A model flow over HTTP involves a client machine, which will request a server which will then send a message in response. The way an Internet communications platform, for instance, a web browser, asks for information is through an HTTP, this information is then used to load websites. With every HTTP request made across the Internet, there is a series of encoded data that carries different forms of information.

title: intro
text:
ISP
(ISP) otherwise known as an Internet service provider, provides myriad services that allow you to access, use, manage, or participate in the Internet. ISPs are organized in many forms ex: commercial, community-owned, or non-profit, they can be privately owned as well. Many Internet services are provided by ISPs. These include but are not limited to internet access, internet transit, domain name registration, web hosting, and colocation.

title: intro
text:
DNS
The Domain Name System’s (DNS) job is to turn a domain name into an IP address, which is then used by internet browsers to load internet pages. All devices that are connected to the Internet have an IP address, these IP addresses are used by other devices to locate the device. DNS servers make it possible for people to input normal words into their browser, an example being Youtube.com, without needing to keep track of the IP address of said website. For this to work, the URL typed must go through four servers for the IP address to be provided.

Software Infrastructure
To run a computer you are gonna need an operating system. It manages memory and processes as well as the computer’s software and hardware. You’ll also need server software. Server software simplifies data storage, communications, applications and other functions. It handles tasks like load balancing, security protocols, database management and more.

What categories are there?
There are two main categories of software:
The first category is system software. It is what works with and runs the computer’s hardware. It manages memory, devices and processors. System software is constantly working while a device is running. It is the base for application software.
The second is application software. Application software performs a specific task for the user. Some examples would be Google Chrome or Firefox. It can range from communication apps to games like Candy Crush. Application software needs system software to run while system software can run independently.

title: Hosting, Clients, & Servers
text:
What is Web Hosting?
Web hosting is a service that allows individuals and organizations to make their websites accessible on the internet. When creating a website, all of the files, images, and other content need to be stored somewhere so that people can access them online. Web hosting companies provide the technology and server space needed to store these files and keep your website running smoothly. There are a couple different types of web hosting services, such as shared hosting, where multiple websites share the same server. These servers also tend to be less expensive because the resources are shared with other website owners. Dedicated hosting is where a single website has an entire server to itself. The choice of what hosting service you need depends on the website’s needs, such as the amount of traffic it expects and the level of control required. Essentially, without web hosting, your website wouldn’t be viewable by users on the internet.

What Are Web Clients?
A web client is a software application used to interact with web servers and access web content. When you use a web browser like Chrome, Firefox, or Safari to visit a website, that browser acts as a web client. It sends requests to web servers asking for specific web pages or resources, and the server responds by sending the requested data back to the client. The client then processes and displays the information on your screen. Web clients can also include other applications, such as mobile apps, that access web services to retrieve data or perform actions. Essentially, the web client is the interface that allows users to interact with the massive amounts of resources available on the internet.


What is a Web Server?
A web server is a computer system that hosts websites and delivers web pages to users over the internet. When you type a web address into your browser, the browser sends a request to a web server where the website is stored. The server then processes this request then sends back the needed web pages, images, and other resources to your browser, which displays them for you to see on your screen. Web servers are filled with the necessary software that manages these requests and ensures that the correct data is sent to the right user. They also handle multiple requests at the same time, making it possible for many users to access the same website at the same time. Essentially, web servers are a central part of the internet, enabling users to access and interact with the web content smoothly.

title: static site generators
text:
Different static site generators

Jekyll
Created in 2008 by a Github employee, this model is largely used and known due to its integration into Github. Jekyll renders either Textile or Markdown to produce a static site. Github pages offers free hosting when Jekyll is used alongside it, domain name and all.


Hugo
Hugo takes data files, i18n bundles, assets, and content written in HTML, Markdown etc, and renders a static site. It is the fastest renderer on the market, running at 1ms or less per page. Most sites take less than one second to render. Hugo is open source, meaning that there will always be improvement and flexibility.


11ty
11ty does not require a Javascript framework, meaning a zero client-side javascript across the board by default. With 11ty you can work from a foundation of prerendered templates that suit your project. 11ty works with your project’s existing directory structure. The tool doesn’t require any type of directory, use the structure you want.
